kai: morning - quick proposal: build a tiny 'fallback agent' service that makes per-request decisions for canaries. goal: deterministic, explainable, and low-latency.
meera: short Q: agent vs gateway? why separate from rollout controller?
kai: agent = runtime-facing, stateless decision evaluator. rollout controller owns policies and versions. agent fetches policies and evaluates against recent signals. separation keeps control-plane simple.
oliver: signals: runtime sends minimal envelope (p95,p99,err_rate,cache_hit,model_score_hint). agent subscribes to pre-aggregated windows or accepts quick_signals for very hot paths.
meera: need hysteresis + sticky semantics. propose agent returns {actions, ttl, sticky_token?}. runtime stores sticky_token locally with its own TTL.
ops_bot: ops: ensure audit trail + debug endpoint. Also fail-open default so production doesn't panic if agent unreachable.
deploy-bot: canary: fallback-agent-proto -> staging (build 421).
kai: example actions: NOOP, MIRROR, SWITCH_VARIANT:quantized-v1, REROUTE_PERCENT(10), SERVE_STUB. compound allowed.
meera: testing: replay historical metric windows and a chaos harness. start with subset of tenants.
oliver: I'll sketch a tiny DSL for rules in the RFC. keeps weights and banded thresholds.
kai: thanks all, I'll post RFC with sample API and telemetry contract later.
